thread:
lucy: Quick heads-up — AcmeHealth go‑live set for TOMORROW 12:00 PT. SI (Ana) hit two blockers: customer firewall blocks egress to our telemetry endpoint, and they need guidance on cert rotation for private deployment. Can we do a rapid arch check?

ana: We discovered the health cluster can't reach 'events.redwood.internal' on 443. Partner asked for a temporary workaround so they can start ingesting logs.

raj: Do we have the exact outbound IPs/ports they need to allow?

marco: Ports are minimal: 443 and 8443 for our health websocket. If they can't open 443 outbound we can tunnel over 8443 but need network config from their infra team.

lucy: @olivia from Acme shared these notes —
olivia: FYI their infra team only allows predefined CIDR ranges; they won't open wide ranges. They asked if we can provide static egress IPs or a VPC endpoint.

raj: Static egress IPs: possible on Dedicated customers with NAT gateway reserved pools. For marketplace/private we can offer a private link endpoint — requires infra change on their side.

ana: Also the client asked about cert rotation: their Compliance needs signed cert chain from our CA or a CSR flow. Current image expects cert at /etc/redwood/tls/server.pem.

sam: Eng‑security here — we can support CSR flow. Need CSR + validity window. We can produce short‑lived certs (~24h) for the go‑live and schedule full rotation afterwards. ETA ~2h once CSR provided.

marco: For immediate unblock: 1) If they can add a single outbound rule to allow our NAT IP 52.11.22.33 -> 443/8443, that unblocks telemetry. 2) If not, we can set up an SSH tunnel from their bastion to a relay host we control (temporary). Which does the partner prefer?

olivia: Bastion tunnel is doable but needs approval from our security lead. I'll escalate that now. If we go the IP route, can Redwood guarantee that IP won't change during the maintenance window?

raj: We can provision an Elastic NAT and tag it for this customer for 48h, but must note it's not a long‑term SLA. I'll start the request with infra.

lucy: Also note a marketplace image size issue — their airgapped deployment can't pull from public registries. They need a signed image tarball. Is there a signed artifact we can hand to field?

marco: Yes — we can export the image and sign with our image‑signing key. I'll generate a signed tarball and upload to secure drop. ETA 3h.

ana: That would unblock their on‑prem install path. Please include checksum and signature instructions in the artifact readme.

sam: Quick checklist from security: 1) CSR received 2) Validity window 3) Signed image checksum 4) IP whitelisting confirmation. Send all to secure@redwood and cc me.

olivia: I'm on it. Sending CSR and approval thread to secure@redwood in the next 30m.

raj: I'll open a short‑lived NAT and ping infra to expedite. If anyone needs me to file infra tickets, ping me. :thumbsup:

marco: Putting a small runbook snippet here for the on‑prem team —
```
# temporary firewall rule
allow outbound to 52.11.22.33 ports 443,8443 proto TCP
# image install (on airgapped host)
tar xvf redwood-image-acme-2026-03.tar.gz
sudo cp server.pem /etc/redwood/tls/
redwoodctl start
```

lucy: Thanks team. I'll coordinate with Ana and Olivia, and post updates here. If Sam or Raj need any approvals, call me.

ana: Acme just confirmed security lead is looking at the bastion tunnel. If they deny, we'll go NAT + signed image.

olivia: Sent CSR + approval to secure@redwood. Also uploaded network topology diagram to the shared folder: https://acme.share/rg/infra/topology.pdf

sam: Got the CSR — processing now. Will reply with signed cert and expiry details in ~90m.

marco: Image tarball started upload to secure drop: https://secure.redwood/drops/acme-2026-03 (private link). ETA 2.5h.

raj: NAT request submitted: INC-58921. Tagging @infra. Putting expected IP in the ticket.

lucy: Great — let's aim for a final check at 10:30 PT tomorrow morning. If anything changes, update this thread. :calendar: 

ana: Copy that, thanks everyone.
